parole.significato: bonfire that is lit as a signal, e.g. to warn of war, invasions etc. typically on top of a hill.
parole.testo: From Old Danish baghn from Old Frisian baken. cognates include English beacon, West Frisian beaken. Related to båke.

From Old Danish fanden, fænden, probably borrowed from Old Frisian fandiand, a present participle of fandia (“to tempt”), from Proto-Germanic *fandōną (“to find out”), cognate with Old English fandian (“to try, tempt”), German fahnden (“to search”). Late Old Norse fendinn, Norwegian faen, and Swedis
From Old Frisian gāst, from Proto-West Germanic *gaist. Doublet of gejst.
